title: ParkFlow demo video
vo: Every weekend, mall car parks fill up.
And the first thing a loyal member does at the mall is circle for a space.
This is ParkFlow.
Reserve capacity, not parking bays.
Malaysia has 988 shopping complexes, and every one wants its members to feel valued.
But today, parking privileges mean permanent VIP bays that sit empty off-peak while shoppers circle below,
or bay locks and sensors on every reserved space, costly to install and maintain.
So we asked:
why should parking privileges cost parking efficiency?
Take the same twenty bays: two members parked, two on the way, sixteen shoppers.
Bay locks leave four bays empty and two shoppers waiting.
A VIP zone is worse: six empty bays, four shoppers waiting.
ParkFlow pools the zone.
Members are guaranteed a share of capacity, not a specific bay,
so nobody waits and no hardware goes in the bays.
One rule runs the gate.
Public entry capacity equals total capacity, minus cars already parked, minus confirmed members still on the way, minus a safety margin.
One hundred, minus seventy-five, minus twenty, minus five, leaves zero.
The sign turns amber.
Shoppers are guided to another zone, and confirmed members drive in after a number-plate check.
It runs on parts malls already own.
CCTV estimates occupancy; ANPR at the gate keeps a second count.
The operator sets each zone's member quota.
Bookings are confirmed only after membership, overlap, capacity and quota checks.
Every car meets the gate rule.
And if a member doesn't show, the grace period ends and the space goes back to everyone.
Here is the working prototype: the ParkFlow command centre, running a three-level car park in simulation.
Across the top: occupancy, gate-to-park time, cars still searching, and arrivals expected in the next thirty minutes.
The live 3D twin shows every car and every bay light: green free, red taken, pink for Ladies' parking, gold for members, blue for accessible bays.
Click a car to see its route, and exactly why ParkFlow sent it to that zone.
A board counts free bays on each level.
Below: the next thirty minutes of arrivals and departures,
and a timestamped log of every gate decision.
The Forecast tab predicts demand from history plus cinema, dining and events,
and shows the membership team how many parked cars are members, live and since opening.
Reservations manages the special bays.
Ladies' parking and designated member bays can be booked within capacity.
Accessible OKU bays are protected and never sold.
And Impact proves it.
The same weekend surge, 136 cars, runs twice on identical demand.
With guidance, gate-to-park time falls 44 percent, and search driving falls 32 percent,
along with the tailpipe emissions it causes.
Drivers see the same picture on their phone.
Before leaving, they check free bays by level.
“I’m on my way” gives turn-by-turn guidance straight to a zone.
Members reserve with a ten-minute grace period, and women drivers can book Ladies' parking.
Then: find my car, and pay by e-wallet, card or member points.
The impact is measurable from day one.
Members get parking they can rely on.
Every shopper spends less time searching, and keeps every uncommitted space.
Malls get a benefit members feel on every visit, with no bay hardware.
And less search driving means fewer emissions inside the car park.
That's SDG 11, sustainable cities and communities, supported by SDG 9.
And it's ready to pilot.
Phase one, this prototype, is done.
Phase two: one zone in one mall, using the CCTV, ANPR and gate already installed.
Then we measure, improve, and scale to mixed-use developments and township car parks.
We'll test camera blind spots, data privacy under the PDPA, and overstays in the open.
It pays for itself three ways:
an operator software licence, premium membership upgrades, and optional paid reservations at peak times.
Start with one zone; the same software runs in any of Malaysia's 988 malls.
ParkFlow.
Better parking privileges. Smarter space utilisation. Stronger membership value.
